# What `lib/app.g.dart` contains

As of v0.13.0 (`cli/templates/app.g.dart.jinja`). One plain go_router plus
Riverpod file, meant to be read and committed. It never names your types
except for a typed `extra` and enum segments or query parameters, which it
imports by name (`import '...' show Category;`). Everything else flows through
inference.

## The header

```text
// GENERATED by fespalier from lib/app/. Do not edit; run `fsp gen`.
// ignore_for_file: type=lint, unused_import, unused_element
//
//   /           HomeRoute   page.dart  (layout, transition)
//   /items/:id  ItemRoute   items/$id/page.dart  (data, transition)
```

The route table in the comment is what `fsp routes` prints. Files are imported
as `_i0`, `_i1`, ...; a `$` in a path is escaped (`items/\$id/page.dart`).

## `AppRoutes`

| Member                                                                           | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `router({initialLocation, launch, observers, restorationScopeId, navigatorKey})` | A whole `GoRouter` for `MaterialApp.router(routerConfig:)`, built with `GoRouter.routingConfig` (since 0.19.0) over the routing config a debug hot reload swaps (see "Hot reload" below). Passes `extraCodec:` when `extra_codec.dart` exists, and `errorBuilder` shows `routing.notFound(uri)`. **No `refreshListenable`**. `launch` (an `InboundLaunch`, since 0.11.0) is where the app was opened from; the router is built inside `launchRouter` |
| `mount({at = '/', navigatorKey})`                                                | The routes alone (`List<RouteBase>`), to put inside your own `GoRouter`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `base`                                                                           | Where the tree is mounted: `'/'`, or the `at` given to `mount`. Typed routes read it, so `.location` stays right under a prefix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `rootNavigatorKey`                                                               | The root navigator's `GlobalKey<NavigatorState>`: the one you supplied to the last `router()` or `mount()`, else a fresh one that call made                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `notFound(uri)`                                                                  | The nearest `not_found.dart` to `uri` (what `errorBuilder` calls)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `matchUrl(uri)` / `dataAt(uri)`                                                  | A `UrlMatch?` / the data providers, outermost first. No guard runs, no widget is built. `null`: no route, or a segment did not parse                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `urlOf(route, {locale})`                                                         | Only with a `links:` section whose first domain is usable (since 0.16.0): `Uri.parse('https://<first domain>${route.locationFor(locale)}')`, the mount prefix included. See `cli-and-config.md`, "`fsp links`"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `deferred`, `loadDeferred()`                                                     | Only in an app with a deferred route (since 0.7.0): the `DeferredLibrary` of each, and a call that loads them all (see "Deferred pages")                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `preload(ref, uri, {keepFor})`                                                   | The page's data (and, when deferred, its code) behind one `PrefetchHandle`; a location that matches no route gets a closed handle                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `attach(router[, container])`, `onEnter(...)`                                    | Only in an app with `observe.dart`, `telemetry: true` or `adapters:` (`attach`), and with `adapters:` (`onEnter`, go_router's, since 0.11.0): see "Pieces that depend on the app" below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `all`, `byType`, `byPath`, `match(uri)`                                          | Forwarded from `AppManifest` (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

`mount` **stores** `at` and `navigatorKey` in static fields, so the last call
wins. `router()` calls `mount()` itself. **Since 0.5.0 a call without a
`navigatorKey` makes a fresh key** instead of keeping the one an earlier call
stored (on 0.4.x and earlier it kept it, so a test could see another test's key),
and a bare `AppRoutes.mount()` therefore restores both defaults (`base` `'/'`, a
new key): end a test that mounted under a prefix with `addTearDown(AppRoutes.mount)`.

## Pieces that depend on the app

- **`AppAdapters`** (a class beside `AppRoutes`, only with `adapters:`, since 0.11.0): `zone`, `beforeRun`, `launch`,
  `overrides`, `providerObservers`, `routerObservers` and `wrap`, each forwarding to the `FespalierAdapters` the pubspec's
  list builds; `main: manual` apps call it (`app-main.md`).
- **`AppRoutes.attach(router[, container])`** (only with `observe.dart`, `telemetry: true` or `adapters:`): `router()` calls
  it without a container, and it makes `devToolsAttach`, the `observe.dart` hooks (`observeAttach`, with the container),
  `telemetryAttach` and each adapter's `attach` (with the container, once per router) follow that router. An app
  that builds its own `GoRouter` calls it once with that router (`fespalier-migration`).
- **`AppRoutes.onEnter`** (only with `adapters:`): go_router's `onEnter`, the `FespalierAdapter.onEnter` getter's function of each
  adapter that has one (since 0.16.0), in the pubspec's order. `AppRoutes.router` passes it as
  `onEnter: AppAdapters.handlesEnter ? onEnter : null`, so only an app with an adapter that has one gets it; an app with
  a router of its own passes the same. Without one (and without adapters, where it does not exist) an app keeps
  go_router's simplest path (any `onEnter` makes go_router parse every navigation asynchronously). `AppAdapters.handlesEnter`
  is true when any adapter's getter is not null, and `launchRouter` gets `links: AppAdapters.handlesEnter` with adapters and no telemetry.
- **`enum <Name>Step`** (since 0.11.0): the steps of a multi-page form, one per step folder (`fespalier-data`).

## `AppManifest`

`all` (a `const` list of `RouteInfo`, in route-table order), `byType` (typed
route class to info), `byPath` (path template to info; since 0.19.0 both are getters over `routeIndex(all)`, built once for the list and built again by a hot reload), `of(GoRouterState)` (the
route a layout is showing; `null` in a not-found view) and `match(uri)`. With
`output_manifest:` it lives in its own library (`AppRoutes.all`, `byType`,
`byPath`, `match` then exist only if the manifest is in `app.g.dart`; import the
manifest library and use `AppManifest` instead, which has the same name in both
modes). `AppRoutes.matchUrl` and `dataAt` always stay in `app.g.dart`.

## Typed routes

Every page and redirect gets a `final class XRoute extends TypedLocation` with a
`const` constructor taking its segments (required) and query parameters
(optional):

```dart
ProductRoute(id: 42).go(context);
const SearchRoute(q: 'ap', page: 2).location;   // /search?q=ap&page=2
```

- `location`: the full location, mount prefix included, canonical spelling; nulls
  and empty lists are left out of the query.
- `locationFor(locale)`, and `locale:` on `go`, `push<T>` and `replace`:
  localized spellings (see `fespalier-routing`).
- `static of(context)` and `static maybeOf(context)` (since 0.5.0): the route at
  the location the widget belongs to, parsed by `AppRoutes.matchUrl`; and, for a
  route with segments or query parameters, `copyWith`, a getter whose type is a
  function with the fields' types (a private `_keep` sentinel behind it tells
  null from omitted). See `fespalier-routing`.
- A route with a typed `extra` has `go`, `push` and `replace` overrides taking
  `extra:`.
- A route with a `data.dart` also has: `static data` (the provider; a family
  when it has keys), `static watch(ref, {keys})`, `static read(ref, {keys})`,
  an **instance** `prefetch(ref, {keepFor})` and an **instance**
  `refresh(ref)`. `watch` and `read` are static on purpose (see
  `fespalier-data`).
- A route with its own data **or a section's above it** also has an instance
  `preload(ref, {keepFor})` (0.5.0): every provider the page reads behind one
  `PrefetchHandle` (`fespalier-data`), and since 0.7.0 the page's code when it is deferred (so a
  deferred route has one even without data). A route with none inherits the base's, which
  returns a closed handle. `AppRoutes.preload(ref, uri, {keepFor})` does it from a
  location, and `RouteLink` (runtime, not generated; `fespalier-routing`) calls it.
- A section's `data.dart` gets `<Folder>Section` with the same five members, all
  static (`fespalier-data`).

## Deferred pages

Since 0.7.0, a route whose folder says `const deferred = true;` (or the pubspec's `deferred: true`) changes
only where its `page.dart` comes from (`fespalier-routing`, `references/route-dart.md`). A route
that isn't deferred is generated byte for byte as before (apart from the page names of 0.9.0, below).

```dart
import 'app/checkout/page.dart' deferred as _i7;      // the page.dart, and nothing else
...
// no data.dart: the page in a DeferredView (never `const`: a deferred class can't be)
DeferredView(
  library: _libCheckout,
  page: () => _i7.CheckoutPage(),
  loading: () => const _i1.RootLoading(),
  error: (e, st, retry) => _i2.RootError(error: e, retry: retry),
)
// a data.dart: the library goes to the DataView, so the code loads with the data
DataView(watch: ..., data: (d) => _i14.ProductPage(product: d), ..., keepPrevious: true, library: _libProductsId)
...
final _libCheckout = DeferredLibrary(_i7.loadLibrary, 'checkout/page.dart');   // one per deferred route, named after its folder (since 0.20.0)
```

- `mount()` registers the libraries (`DeferredLibrary.register(deferred);`), so `pumpRouter` can load them.
- `AppRoutes.deferred` is the list, and `AppRoutes.loadDeferred()` loads all of them.
- The typed route of a deferred route overrides `preload` to call `_libCheckout.preload()` (and keeps its
  providers); `AppRoutes.preload(ref, uri)` is `matchUrl(uri)?.route.preload(ref, keepFor: keepFor) ?? ...`.
- The manifest says `deferred: true` in the route's `RouteInfo`, the header table and `fsp routes`
  tag it `deferred`.

## Page names (since 0.9.0)

Each `pageBuilder:` the file writes (a route with a `transition.dart` or `present.dart`, a `remount` route, a
layout's shell) is wrapped in `namedPage('<pattern>', () => ...)`: two lines per page builder, the first gaining
`namedPage('/products/:id', () =>` and the last a `)`. Everything between keeps its text.

```dart
pageBuilder: (context, state) => namedPage('/products/:id', () => _i3.transition(
  state.pageKey,
  buildWithParams(...),
)),
```

`namedPage` (`package:fespalier/fespalier.dart`) runs its closure once, synchronously, and the pages
`Transitions.*`, `layoutPage` and `remountPage` made inside are named by the pattern: `RouteSettings.name` is
`/products/:id` where it was `null` (a `remount` page: `:id`). A shell is named by its section's pattern (`/` for
a root layout or a `(tabs)/` group). A route with a bare `builder:` is go_router's own page and unchanged; the
typed routes, the manifest, `fsp routes --json` and the DevTools tree do not change. The pattern is the one of
`TelemetrySite.route`. Never edit these lines: `fsp gen` writes them. A `transition.dart` that builds a `Page`
of its own reads the name from `Transitions.pageName`.

## Generated providers

With a `freshness` (since 0.8.1) the body is `freshData(ref, _iN.freshness, traceData(...))` (`_iN` is the `data.dart`, or the
`route.dart` that sets the default), and with a `dataCache` the provider is `cachedData(...)` / `cachedDataFamily(...)`
(`cache: _iN.dataCache`, `name: 'products/\$id'`, `keyParts: (int id) => [id]`, `freshness:` and `retry:` when they
apply). Either adds `keepDataOnError: true` to the route's `DataView`. A route with neither is as in 0.7.0.

A `data()` function becomes `FutureProvider.autoDispose.family(...)` (or
`StreamProvider`). With `data_retry: none` it carries
`retry: (retryCount, error) => null`; with the default `inherit` it sets no
policy, so the app's `ProviderScope(retry:)` applies. A `data.dart` that
exports its own provider (`final data = ...`) or selects one is used as is.

## Scroll restoration (since 0.8.1)

With `scroll_restoration: true` each page's view (inside its transition, under its layouts: the
`DataView`, `DeferredView` or `buildWithParams` call included) is wrapped in
`RouteScrollMemory(state: state, child: ...)`. Layouts, redirects and not-found views are not.
Off, the file has no `RouteScrollMemory`. See `fespalier-layouts`.

## DevTools hooks (since 0.7.0)

The file calls the runtime's DevTools support in four places, all under `if (kFespalierDevTools)`:
`mount()` ends its setup with `devToolsRegister(tree: _devToolsTree, matchUrl: matchUrl)`, `router()` builds the
`GoRouter`, passes it to `devToolsAttach(router)` (through `AppRoutes.attach`, when the app has one) and returns it, `_reload` registers the routes again after a hot reload (since 0.19.0), and `String _devToolsTree()` at the end of the
file returns the route tree (`fsp routes --graph json`) as one string. `kFespalierDevTools` is a `const` that
is false in release builds (and with `--dart-define=fespalier.devtools=false`), so the compiler removes the
calls, the string and the code behind them: a release build has none of it. **Never remove these lines by hand**
(`fsp gen` writes them back); an app that mounts the routes into its own `GoRouter` calls
`devToolsAttach(router)` itself. See the DevTools page of `fespalier-troubleshooting`.

Three more pieces follow the guards, the data and the actions, and they are not under an `if`, because each
returns what it is given: every guard and `redirect.dart` call in a `redirect:` is wrapped as
`traceGuard(state, 'g5@6', <the call>)` (a `redirect.dart`'s site is `r32`; with `guardWithParams` the
whole `guardWithParams(...)` is wrapped, so a bad segment reads `skipped`), the body of a generated
provider as `traceData(ref, 'dProductsId', id, _i4.data(ref, id: id))` (the key is the family's parameter, `k` for
a record of keys, `null` for none; a `data.dart` that returns or selects a provider is not wrapped; with `telemetry: true`,
since 0.9.0, it is `traceDataCall(ref, 'dProductsId', id, () => _i4.data(ref, id: id), telemetry: ...)`, which runs `data()` once,
synchronously, inside the telemetry sink's `within`), and each
action factory gets `site: 'aProductsId_action'`. Since 0.20.0 a data's site is `d` and its folder's stem, and an action's is `a`, its stem, `_` and the function, the suffix of the provider's name, so they stay when a route is added; a guard and a `redirect.dart` keep `g5@6` and `r32`. Since 0.8.1 every `DataView` and `SectionView` reads its data with
`watchData(ref, 'dProductsId', _dataProductsId(v.id))` instead of `ref.watch(...)`, and an app with a `data.dart` has a
function `_devToolsProviders()` (each provider, or family, by site; a selector with parameters is left out)
that `mount()` hands to `devToolsRegister(providers: …)`. The sites are the keys of the tree's `sites`.
`traceGuard`, `traceData`, `traceDataCall` and `watchData` return their last argument (`traceDataCall`: what its
closure returned), the very object (`watchData` returns
`ref.watch(provider)`): a sync guard or `data()` stays sync, a `Future` is not wrapped in another, and in a
release build all three are the identity, inlined away (a release build keeps only the action's `site`
string). Never remove them by hand.

Since 0.8.1, an `action.dart` with companions adds to this: `XRoute.useForm` (a real hook) for a `form()`,
`validate:` and `optimistic:` arguments on the action's factory, and a private `_optimistic<Stem>` layer (`_optimisticItemsId`) for each
`data.dart` an `optimistic()` patches, which the `DataView`, `SectionView` and typed `watch` of that data
read (`ref.watchOptimistic`). Nothing of it is generated for an app without companions. Since 0.11.0 the
file also has `import 'package:fespalier_forms/fespalier_forms.dart';` (after `fespalier/fespalier.dart`),
only when some action has a `form()`; `ActionForm`, `useActionForm` and the rest of what `useForm` calls are
the `fespalier_forms` package's, no longer `fespalier`'s.

## Hot reload (since 0.19.0)

In a debug build, a hot reload after the file was regenerated swaps in the new route table (`reloadRoutes`, which `StartupGate` calls on reassemble). What the file adds for it, and nothing in a profile or release build reads any of it:

- **`_AppRoutesReload`** is a `final class` that extends the runtime's `RoutesReload`. `router()` makes one from `_config(routes)` (a `RoutingConfig` of the routes, and `onEnter` when an adapter has one) and passes it to `GoRouter.routingConfig`, with `routing.follow(router)`. Its methods are the code that is current, so after a reload they read the reloaded `_version`, `_kept` and `AppRoutes._reload`. Nothing goes through a closure made before the reload, which would keep its old code: that is why `router()` builds the routes through these methods.
- **`_version`** is a const hash of the whole file. A reload with the same version swaps nothing, so a page edit costs nothing.
- **`_kept`** is a const map: one hash for each top-level and static `final` of the file (a provider, a deferred library, a `data.dart`'s providers and the `AppRoutes` fields), and `'(router)'`, the settings `router()` is built with (`extraCodec`, `observe`, `attach`, `links`, `push_updates_url`, `semantics_ids`, `telemetry`, the adapters). A name present in both the running file and the reloaded one with another hash refuses the swap, and the app keeps its routes. A new or removed name does not. Since 0.20.0 the generated names follow the folder, not the route's position: `_data<Stem>` (a `data()` function), `_lib<Stem>` (a deferred page), `_optimistic<Stem>` and `_action<Stem>_<function>`, where the stem is the folder in PascalCase (`products/$id` is `ProductsId`, so `_dataProductsId`). Two folders that both have names and the same stem each take `_` and 8 hex digits of a hash of their folder (`order-history/` and `order_history/` give `_dataOrderHistory_a6adc020` and `_dataOrderHistory_5cefc874`). An import alias of a prefixed type is `_e<hash of its library>_<prefix>` (the `package:` URI as written, or the relative one resolved against the importing file and normalized), so it does not change when another file becomes the first to spell a segment's type. So a route added or removed anywhere changes no other name or hash, and a route put before one swaps; a changed `data()` or action, a moved folder that has one (also the second of two folders whose names share a stem, added or removed: it renames the first one's names once, or back), a second deferred route (a page added below a deferred `route.dart` is one), an import prefix pointed at another library and a router setting are still refused. The hashes are computed by `cli/src/reload.rs`, from the generated text, so a new `static final` in the template is covered without a change to the reload.
- **`_keys`** is a `ShellKeys` that each `mount()` makes. A layout's `ShellRoute` takes its `navigatorKey` from it, and a `StatefulShellRoute` its `key` and each branch its `navigatorKey`, by restoration id. The reloaded routes take the same keys, so the pages in a layout keep their state.
- **`_matchers`** is not `final`: `_allMatchers()` makes it, and `_reload` assigns it again. A static that must follow the routes is reassigned in `_reload`, not declared `final`, because a reload keeps the first value of a `final`.
- **`_reload(router)`** calls `devToolsRegister` again, with deferred routes `DeferredLibrary.register(deferred)` (a swap that adds the app's first deferred route puts it in `loadDeferred()` and `anyPending`) and, with `observe.dart`, `observeAttach(router, _observeAt)`; it returns `_config(_routes(_base))`, the routes of the last `mount()`.

`main: manual` apps (even with `AppRoutes.router()` in their own `main()`: `StartupGate`'s `reassemble` starts the swap), and a router of their own around `AppRoutes.mount(at:)`, keep the routes they started with until a restart (`reloadRoutes` is not exported). A rebuild that throws does not use up its version: the next hot reload tries it again. The refused swap's message is in `fespalier-troubleshooting`, "diagnostics-dev".

## What the file does not do

- A guard that takes a `Ref` is called as
  `refGuard(context, 'g8@3', (ref) => _i8.guard(ref, uri: state.uri))` (and a redirect
  that takes one as `refRedirect(context, (ref) => ...)`); one that takes a
  `ProviderContainer` as `_i8.guard(ProviderScope.containerOf(context, listen: false), ...)`,
  as before 0.5.0. The string is a constant naming that guard on that route. Since 0.7.0 each call sits
  inside `traceGuard(state, 'g8@3', ...)`, which returns it unchanged (see above).
- No `redirect` on a plain `ShellRoute`; guards hang on each page's `GoRoute`, and
  go_router runs a matched route's redirect for deep links and navigation inside
  shells, tabs included. The one exception (since 0.11.0): the guards above a tab
  layout run once on its `StatefulShellRoute`'s `redirect:`, not copied into each
  tab's route (a tab's own guard stays on its route).
- A segment that does not parse shows `not_found.dart` and skips the guards that
  read segments or query parameters; a guard that takes neither still runs first.
- Static routes are sorted before dynamic ones before catch-alls at each level,
  so go_router's first match is the most specific.
